source_inspection_notes: Read encode_packed.py in full: flags abi.encodePacked() calls with >1 consecutive dynamic-type (string/bytes/dynamic-array) argument, but ONLY when the argument is 'tainted' (traceable to external/attacker-controllable input via Slither's data-dependency analysis). EthTrust's text has no such taint/exploitability qualifier -- it is an unconditional prohibition on the pattern itself.

derivation_trace.ethtrust_phrase: use abi.encodePacked() with consecutive variable length arguments
derivation_trace.analyzer_behavior: Flags only when the dynamic argument(s) are tainted by external input.
covered_cases: consecutive dynamic args where at least one is attacker-influenceable -- the exploitable case
uncovered_cases: consecutive dynamic args that are internal-only/hardcoded, never externally tainted -- still literally matches EthTrust's unconditional text, never flagged by this detector
derivation_trace.final_classification: PARTIAL_MATCH -- this is the one requirement in this batch with NO override clause, so if a fully-matching predicate existed it could reach EXACT_MATCH; the taint-filter gap is what keeps it at PARTIAL, not an override ambiguity.
